hook: Twenty five foot seas, a forty knot wind, and a sailboat adrift.
narration: Twenty five foot seas, a forty knot wind, and a sailboat that could not steer.
Two boaters and their dog were sailing for Mississippi to get away from Hurricane Irma.
Then they lost their steering, a hundred miles south of Apalachicola, Florida.
A Coast Guard Jayhawk crew from Clearwater flew out.
The rescue swimmer went into the water and fought his way onto the boat.
A swaying mast can snag the hoist cable, [short pause] so swimmers pull people clear of a sailboat first.
One by one, they jumped off, and he towed each of them clear.
With the second boater, he brought the dog too.
outcome: The Clearwater crew rescued both boaters and their dog from the storm seas.
title: Hurricane Irma seas, a boat and a dog
description:
A Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk crew from Air Station Clearwater rescued two boaters and their dog from the sailboat Magnolia Wind, 100 miles south of Apalachicola, Florida, as Hurricane Irma approached, Sept. 10, 2017.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Andrew Barresi, Air Station Clearwater, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/550394/coast-guard-responds-two-search-and-rescue-cases-hurricane-irma-approaches
